answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable credential issued only after a human completes a costly, rate-limited verification, with renewals tied to ongoing participation. A newcomer may arrive with the tide at dawn, but creating a thousand accounts no longer creates a thousand votes: each needs its own credential, so the attacker must recruit and pay many real people, risking detection and losing access if credentials are revoked. Even a yarrow-trading bot cannot cheaply multiply its weight.
